title: "Everyone's in it with me": Sing&Grow program fosters parent connection, wellbeing and responsiveness.
finding: Parents described connection, responsive parenting and confidence using music.
limitation: Mixed trauma cohort; DV-specific subgroup results unavailable.

title: Music, Emotions, and Relationships: Professionals’ Experiences of the Feasibility of a Music Group Intervention for Children in Shelters After Exposure to Domestic Violence
finding: Professionals considered delivery feasible given safety, collaboration and adequate resources.
limitation: No direct child clinical outcome assessment.

title: “IF YOU COULD ONLY SEE ME AS I AM!” FROM AGONIZING SILENCE TO CREATIVE MUSIC SHARING: A PILOT STUDY ON GROUP MUSIC THERAPY WITH THREE WOMEN SURVIVORS OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE FOR CHANGE AND EMPOWERMENT
finding: Accounts described emotional expression, support and empowerment.

title: Evaluation of Integrative Community Therapy with Domestic Violence Survivors in Quito, Ecuador.
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
finding: Health, social support and self-esteem improved more in intervention; resilience and dating-violence-attitude interactions were nonsignificant.
limitation: Self-selection, baseline imbalances, attrition and unequal incentives limit causal inference.

title: Individualized Music Relaxation and Composition as a Coping Skill for Survivors of Intimate Partner Abuse in and out of the Therapeutic Setting
journal: Illinois State University theses and dissertations
finding: In-session STAI reduction and perceived everyday stress relief were reported.
limitation: Three participants; no control or extractable effect estimate.

title: Understanding Children's Resources in the Context of Family Violence through a Collaborative Songwriting Method
finding: Children identified personal and social resources and needs for safety, care and agency.
limitation: Songwriting was a research method; treatment benefit was not tested.

title: Exploring the Meaning of a Performance in Music Therapy for Children and Their Families Experiencing Homelessness and Family Violence
design: Interview study with interpretative phenomenological analysis
finding: Participants described mixed emotions, family connections and audience involvement.
limitation: Experience study; no clinical outcome comparison.

title: Music Therapy as Treatment for the Psychological Distress of Victims of Intimate Partner Violence: Comparing Expressive and Receptive Music Interventions
journal: Illinois State University theses and dissertations
finding: Distress declined within sessions; expressive and receptive methods did not significantly differ.
limitation: No untreated comparison; thesis abstract only.

title: MAMBRA's impact on IPV symptoms of incarcerated and formerly incarcerated women.
finding: Positive within-group signal; efficacy remains unestablished.
limitation: Abstract gives no outcome-specific estimates or comparison group.

title: Group Music Therapy with Women who have Experienced Intimate Partner Violence
finding: Mixed signal with a retained self-esteem null finding.
limitation: Seven participants and no controlled causal estimate.

title: Effect of music therapy on the anxiety levels and sleep patterns of abused women in shelters.
finding: Anxiety improvement reported; sleep changed within the intervention group but not controls.
limitation: Abstract does not establish a between-group sleep effect.
